headline: OpenAI expands Trusted Access with GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5-Cyber for enhanced cybersecurity.

items.title: Running Codex safely at OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI has implemented a secure environment for running Codex, utilizing sandboxing, approval processes, network policies, and agent-native telemetry. These measures ensure that Codex operates safely and complies with adoption standards for coding agents. This approach is part of OpenAI's efforts to maintain high-security standards while allowing developers to leverage Codex for enhanced coding capabilities without compromising safety.
items.why_it_matters: Ensuring the safe and compliant use of Codex is critical for developers integrating AI coding agents into secure environments.

items.title: Scaling Trusted Access for Cyber with GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5-Cyber
items.summary: OpenAI has expanded its Trusted Access initiative by introducing GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5-Cyber, two models designed to enhance cybersecurity capabilities. These models assist verified defenders in accelerating vulnerability research and protecting critical infrastructure. The new models are tailored for cybersecurity experts, enabling them to conduct more effective and efficient investigations and offer robust protection measures.
items.why_it_matters: Incorporating AI models into cybersecurity workflows can significantly boost a developer's ability to safeguard systems against emerging threats.

items.title: Advancing voice intelligence with new models in the API
items.summary: OpenAI has released new real-time voice models in its API, which can perform reasoning, translation, and transcription of speech. These models aim to provide more natural and intelligent voice interactions, enhancing user experiences in applications that rely on voice input and processing.

items.title: Secure short-term GPU capacity for ML workloads with EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and SageMaker training plans
items.summary: Amazon has introduced EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML and SageMaker training plans, providing a solution to secure short-term GPU capacity for machine learning workloads. This service addresses the challenge of GPU availability, allowing users to reserve capacity for load testing and short-duration projects.

items.title: Streaming Tokens and Tools: Multi-Turn Agentic Harness Support in NVIDIA Dynamo
items.summary: NVIDIA has enhanced its Dynamo platform with multi-turn agentic harness support, enabling complex agent interactions and efficient token streaming. This update facilitates the development of more interactive and responsive AI systems, particularly in applications requiring continuous dialogue and interaction.

items.title: Adaptive Parallel Reasoning: The Next Paradigm in Efficient Inference Scaling
items.summary: Researchers at Berkeley introduce adaptive parallel reasoning, a novel approach to enhance the efficiency of inference scaling in AI models. This method allows for the distribution of computational tasks across multiple processors, improving speed and accuracy in AI reasoning processes.
items.source: The Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Research Blog

items.title: BALAR : A Bayesian Agentic Loop for Active Reasoning
items.summary: The BALAR framework proposes a Bayesian loop model that enhances active reasoning in AI systems. This model enables interactive AI agents to engage in multi-round information exchange, improving their ability to reason about tasks and adapt to user interactions.

items.title: Improving token efficiency in GitHub Agentic Workflows
items.summary: GitHub has shared methods for enhancing token efficiency in agentic workflows, which are crucial for reducing API costs in production environments. By optimizing these workflows, developers can mitigate large API bills accumulated from frequent pull request runs.
items.source: The latest on AI & ML - The GitHub Blog
